en: The Hymn to the Five-Syllabled Mantra of Śiva

Salutations to Śiva, who is worshipped by all the Vedas, Purāṇas, and holy Āgamas born from the syllable Oṃ; whose pleasing appearance takes the form of the syllable Oṃ, and who himself is the form of the syllable Oṃ. Salutations to the Lord who destroys various old age and diseases, who is the refuge of the world, and who acts for the welfare of the universe.
To that syllable *Na*, which demonstrates the knowledge of various arts...
2. To that syllable *Ma*, which arises as the destroyer of the fault of envy, which wards off the suffering of mother and father, and which is the eternal, subtle boon of Maheśvarī... 3.
To him who is firm in his vows of morality, penance, and knowledge; who is like pure gold in character; who is ever-striving;
who is swift; who is eternally served by the gods; to that Śikāra...
[4] To him whose splendor is like lightning in the left half [of his body]; who brings liberation through speech, mind, and action.
...to that syllable *Va*, which is eternally for the sake of Vāgīśvarī, the Subtle One, and the Excellent One;

[5] to that syllable *Ya*, which is the vow of the gods such as the lords of Yakṣas and Uragas, which is the object of the eyes of the women of the Yakṣas, and which exists for the welfare of the world among the worlds of the Yakṣas. [6]

Salutations to her whose eyes are like blooming blue lotuses; salutations to her whose eyes are fire, moon, and sun; salutations to the sovereign of all, who is herself without a lord; and salutations to Śiva... 7.
Thus ends the hymn of the five syllables of Śiva.
